question: Which developmental stage matches the highest rate of human physical growth after infancy?
explanation: Adolescence is characterized by a rapid growth spurt second only to the infancy period. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h1)

question: Why do nutritional demands peak during the teenage years?

options.A: Rapid increases in height and body mass occur
options.B: Teens stop consuming family meals altogether
options.C: Metabolic rates drop significantly during puberty

explanation: Dramatic shifts in height, weight, and body composition require higher energy and nutrient inputs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h1)

question: What percentage of daily calories should come from carbohydrates for teenagers?
explanation: Carbohydrates form the bulk of daily energy needs to fuel both physical activity and brain function. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h2)

question: A nursing care plan for an active adolescent should emphasize dietary fats primarily for which reason?

options.A: Replacing the need for daily protein intake
options.B: Accelerating immediate water absorption in the gut
options.C: Supporting hormone production and neurological development
options.D: Preventing all forms of acute gastrointestinal illness

explanation: Healthy dietary fats play a vital structural and regulatory role in adolescent endocrine and nervous systems. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h2)

question: Adolescent girls require extra iron intake primarily to compensate for which normal physiological process?
explanation: Monthly menstrual blood loss increases iron requirements in adolescent females. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h3)

question: A 14-year-old girl presents with fatigue and poor dietary intake of dairy products. Which long-term risk should the nurse watch out for?

options.A: Reduced peak bone mass leading to osteoporosis
options.B: Immediate shrinkage of skeletal muscle tissue
options.C: Total loss of pancreatic enzyme activity
options.D: Permanent cessation of normal brain development

explanation: Inadequate calcium intake during the adolescent bone-building window compromises lifelong skeletal strength. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h3)

question: What indicates that an adolescent is already experiencing a fluid deficit during sports?

options.B: Painful muscle cramps in the legs
options.D: A sudden spike in body temperature

explanation: Thirst acts as a delayed physiological signal, meaning fluid loss has already started by the time it is felt. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h4)

question: Why are sugary carbonated beverages discouraged for rehydrating active teenagers?

options.A: They completely stop the body from producing sweat
options.B: They absorb into the bloodstream much faster than water
options.C: They can cause energy crashes and dental caries
options.D: They permanently damage the kidneys within minutes

explanation: High sugar content promotes tooth decay and erratic blood glucose levels instead of steady hydration. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h4)

question: Which meal is most frequently skipped by adolescents, contributing to poor nutrient intake?
explanation: Breakfast is the most commonly missed meal among teenagers due to morning rushes and academic schedules. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h5)

question: A teenager frequently consumes fast foods high in empty calories while skipping meals. What is the most likely outcome of this pattern?

options.A: Enhanced physical endurance during sports events
options.B: Excessive accumulation of dense bone mineral tissue
options.C: Micronutrient deficiencies despite adequate total energy
options.D: Permanent stabilization of normal blood pressure levels

explanation: Fast foods provide calories but lack essential vitamins and minerals, leading to hidden deficiencies. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h5)

question: Why should nurses focus on short-term benefits like sports performance when counseling teenagers?

options.A: Adolescents lack the legal right to make any personal health choices
options.B: Long-term health concepts are too complex for human brains to grasp
options.C: Teens respond better to immediate, tangible outcomes than distant disease risks
options.D: Chronic diseases never develop until a person reaches old age

explanation: Adolescents are future-oriented to a lesser degree, making immediate perks more persuasive motivators. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h6)

question: During a clinic visit, a nurse wants to improve dietary adherence for a teenage patient. Which strategy is most effective?

options.A: Directing all dietary instructions exclusively to the accompanying parent
options.B: Handing over a strict international meal plan with imported ingredients
options.C: Warning the teenager about severe medical conditions in old age
options.D: Involving the teenager directly and suggesting local, affordable food options

explanation: Empowering the teen with realistic, culturally relevant choices fosters better long-term dietary habits. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h6)
